etymologies.etymologyHTML: From fog +‎ -y, originally in the sense "covered with tall grass; marshy; thick". It is not clear whether fog (“mist”) is a back-formation from foggy (“covered with tall, obscuring grass”) or has a separate Germanic origin, and hence whether foggy (“covered with tall grass”) and foggy (“obscured by mist”) represent one word or two. See fog ("mist"; "tall grass") for more.

definitions.definition: Obscured by mist or fog; unclear; hazy

quote.citation: 1960, P. G. Wodehouse, Jeeves in the Offing, chapter VI:
quote.text: If she knew [a psychiatrist was] observing her son with a view to finding out if he was foggy between the ears, there would be umbrage on her part, or even dudgeon.

definitions.definition: Being, covered with, or pertaining to fog (“tall grass etc that grows after, or is left after, cutting; moss”)

quote.citation: 1680, Leonard Mascall, The government of cattel. Divided into three books, etc, page 221:
quote.text: For they will feed on foggy grass and such like. Also ye shall understand that horses and Cattel may not well be foddered in Winter all together, but  […]
[…]  for as he shuts up his meadow at Christmas, leaves such foggy grass behind, and manures well, in case a wet hot summer succeeds,  […]

quote.citation: 1808, John Stagg, Miscellaneous Poems, Some of which are in the Cumberland and Scottish Dialects, page 143:
quote.text: See swingin' owr the foggy swaird, Begrac'd wi' angel features,  […]
